[NatWest demo] Chaos injection audit.description:
Emits ONE ITSI notable for every nwpay:chaos event (action=inject or action=clear) so each incident.sh subcommand AND every click on the SPA Chaos Dashboard surfaces a row in Episode Review (ITSI Event Analytics). This is the SOC-on-stage signal that the audience watches scroll past as the presenter triggers scenarios: detection-and-attribution evidence that every production-touching action was logged AND classified by the SIEM, regardless of who triggered it (presenter via SPA, ops via CLI, or chaos-controller itself during recover()).

Severity mapping:
  * inject -> high (5)   (a new chaos is in progress; opens an Episode)
  * clear  -> info (1)   (chaos resolved; attaches to the open Episode as the 'all clear' marker)

Service mapping (drives Episode grouping and which L2 tile turns red):
  * api-gateway + details.tier=bronze/silver/gold -> Customer Tier Experience
  * fraud-detection-service + scenario=gold-fast-path-off -> Customer Tier Experience
  * fraud-detection-service, sanctions-aml-service -> Business Services
  * payment-*-service                              -> Payment Services
  * swift-network and other *-network              -> Payment Networks
  * ledger-service, postgres, redis, kafka         -> Ledger & Settlement Services
  * traffic-generator (madrid-network-degradation) -> Payments by Location
  * multi (recover-all)                            -> NatWest Card Payments (L1)
  * fallback                                       -> NatWest Card Payments

Dedupe: cohort_key is bound to the HEC-issued event_id, which is unique per call from both incident.sh AND chaos-controller/app/audit.py, so a re-run of this search inside the 3-minute lookback can never double-emit. The complementary chaos_off_change_window.json correlation search continues to emit a SECOND notable when an inject happens outside Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00 UTC; the two notables roll up into the same Episode (correlation_field=service in payments_episode_policy.json) so Episode Review shows one ticket with two attached events: 'chaos was injected' + 'chaos was injected OFF-WINDOW'. That dual signal is intentional - the compliance story benefits from seeing both detections.

[NatWest demo] Chaos injection outside c.action.itsi_event_generator.param.title: $result.title$
[NatWest demo] Chaos injection outside c.description: Detects chaos-audit events (nwpay:chaos action=inject) landing OUTSIDE the published change window (Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00 UTC). Demonstrates the SOC-style discipline of treating any production-touching action outside the agreed change window as a SIEM-grade signal, even when the actor is a legitimate operator. Fires one ITSI notable per inject so the platform team can verify it was an approved exception (a 'normal' inject inside the window does not fire). The actor and scenario travel on the notable event so Episode Review has the context to triage without re-running the search.

[NatWest demo] Payments - cross-source c.description:
MULTI-SOURCE narrative correlation. Joins SIX independent telemetry sources (client-side simulated RTT, backend gateway server-span p95, application ERROR logs, Splunk Observability detector firings, active chaos scenarios, ThousandEyes synthetic test regressions) on a common (_time-5m-bucket, customer_location) key. Emits a single high-severity notable per region per bucket WHEN at least 2 of the 6 sources confirm a customer-experience incident. The notable carries a pre-narrated bullet description ready for Episode Review, plus structured `signal_*` fields so the operator can see at a glance which sources lit up.

Why this exists: the other correlation searches each describe ONE signal in isolation, which produces a noisy timeline of single-source notables. This one is the 'storyline' notable - it lands LAST (because it needs other signals to already be observed) and provides the cross-source confirmation that elevates an episode from 'probably noise' to 'definitely a real incident'. Paired with the `payments_location_episode_policy` aggregation policy (which splits by customer_location and escalates severity when a storyline notable arrives), this is what transforms the Event Analytics timeline from 'list of facts' into 'narrative grouped by region'.

Sources joined (each is its own subsearch, then unioned via `append` and collapsed via `stats values() by _time, customer_location`):
  A. otel_traces (traffic-generator submit_payment)        -> simulated network RTT p95
  B. otel_traces (api-gateway SPAN_KIND_SERVER)            -> backend p95
  C. otel_logs (severity_text=ERROR)                       -> ERROR log volume
  D. main + splunk_observability:alert                     -> SO Cloud detector firings inferred-tagged with region
  E. otel_traces (chaos-controller scenario.inject)        -> active chaos scenario inferred-tagged with region
  F. thousandeyes (cisco:thousandeyes:trace)               -> ThousandEyes synthetic test regression (errors OR p95>5s) tagged by agent location

Dedup key: storyline:<location>:<5m bucket> - one notable per region per bucket.

Severity ladder (sources confirmed -> ITSI severity):
  2 sources -> 4 (High)
  3 sources -> 5 (Critical)
  4 sources -> 5 (Critical)
  5 sources -> 6 (Critical with auto-escalate)
  6 sources -> 6 (Critical with auto-escalate)

Cron: every 5 minutes (matches the bucket span). Time window: -6m to now to ensure each scheduler tick sees a full settled bucket.

Tuning notes for the operator:
  - The per-source thresholds (rtt_p95 > 800 ms, gw_p95 > 1500 ms, err_n >= 5, te_signal triggers as soon as ANY TE-tagged failure for that region is in the bucket) are deliberately ABOVE the per-source correlation searches' thresholds so this storyline only fires when the situation is genuinely interesting, not on baseline-noise jitter.
  - To get this firing during a demo, run `madrid-network-degradation` for >5 minutes - the chaos scenario alone provides signal E + signal A automatically, and signal D follows ~3 minutes later when the SO Cloud Madrid detector triggers.

[NatWest demo] Payments OTel - settlemen.description:
Reads OTel server spans (index=otel_traces sourcetype=otel:traces service.name=settlement-service kind=SPAN_KIND_SERVER) and counts the volume of consumer-side spans over the last 5 minutes. Fires one ITSI notable when the count drops below 3 (steady-state demo throughput is ~35-50 settlement spans per 5-min bin from the payment-initiation->Kafka->settlement async chain). The signal is a near-zero proxy for two scenarios where the Kafka pipeline breaks but the rest of the chain stays nominally healthy (no api-gateway 5xx, no ledger errors):
  - settlement-producer-off  (KAFKA_PRODUCER_ENABLED=false on payment-initiation-service - no messages reach the topic, settlement spans drop to ~0)
  - kafka-outage             (broker scaled to 0 - producer-side errors might also show up, but the consumer-side silence is the canonical signal)

Why 5 minutes rather than shorter: settlement-service runs a periodic poll loop, so transient blips (single missed poll, broker reconnect) are normal. A 5-minute window with count < 3 is a sustained "the topic is empty" condition, not a single-tick anomaly. Cohort_key groups all firings within the same 5-minute bin into one notable.

Service routing: "Ledger & Settlement Services" so the notable lands in the same Episode as ledger-service / postgres / kafka notables when a meltdown spans multiple layers.

[NatWest demo] ThousandEyes synthetic -.description:
MISSING BRIDGE: every other ITSI correlation search in this repo reads from index=otel_traces / index=otel_logs / index=main. The ThousandEyes Add-on for Splunk ships every synthetic test result into index=thousandeyes (sourcetypes cisco:thousandeyes:trace and cisco:thousandeyes:path-vis), and the Digital Customer Experience (DCE) tier already consumes those events for KPI calculations - but NO correlation search ever turned a TE test failure or latency breach into an ITSI notable event. The result: ThousandEyes data was completely invisible in Episode Review and never participated in the cross-source storyline.

This search closes that gap. It aggregates TE OTLP-flavoured spans per (5-minute bucket, test_name, agent_name) and fires a notable when EITHER:
  - the test had >=2 errored spans in the bucket (status.code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR OR HTTP 5xx), OR
  - the test p95 duration exceeded 5000ms (page-load) / 3000ms (transaction)
The SPL deliberately requires >=3 total spans in the bucket so a single noisy DNS lookup or a single redirect doesn't trip the alert; this matches how a SOC operator would interpret the underlying TE UI.

Why the notable lands in TWO axes:
  - service       = 'Digital Customer Experience'   -> service-axis episode (DCE tile)
  - service_ids   = nwpay_l2_dce,nwpay_l2_payment_by_location,nwpay_l1
                                                    -> the DCE L2 tile + the Payments-by-Location L2 tile both turn amber when a regional agent reports a synthetic failure, AND the L1 NatWest Card Payments rolls up
  - customer_location = lowercase city extracted from agent_name (london / madrid / frankfurt / paris / milan / amsterdam)
                                                    -> the SAME location-axis episode key the location aggregation policy uses, so a TE failure from Madrid lands in the SAME 'Customer experience storyline: madrid' episode as the API gateway p95 breach and the SO Cloud detector

Why this matters during the Madrid demo: the Madrid network-degradation chaos scenario does NOT directly affect the SPA page-load TE tests (they hit our public ingress from external TE agents in London / Amsterdam / Frankfurt, and those agents do NOT traverse the simulated Madrid network link). So in the default chaos, this search will fire on REAL synthetic regressions only - which is the right behaviour for production. To demo TE notables specifically, the operator can either:
  - inject the `chaos-frontend-slowdown` scenario (introduces real SPA latency that TE agents will observe), or
  - run a new TE test from a Madrid agent against the payment-submission API and let the standard madrid chaos make it slow.

Dedupe: cohort_key = te:<test_name>:<agent_name>:<5m bucket>. One notable per (test, agent, bucket) - prevents alert storms when the same regression spans multiple buckets.

Deep link: the notable description includes the TE permalink so the operator can pivot from Episode Review straight into the ThousandEyes UI without a second login.

KNOWN COSMETIC: when a single dispatch produces >1 result row (e.g. London AND Amsterdam both breaching latency in the same 5m bucket), every emitted notable's `title` field is templated from the FIRST result's title. The routing fields (`customer_location`, `service`, `service_ids`, `cohort_key`, `severity`) are correctly per-row, so episode grouping works as designed - it's purely the displayed title that may name a different agent than the one that triggered. This is a Splunk saved-search action limitation with `$result.title$` token substitution, not an ITSI bug. The notable's `description` field (which IS per-row) and the location-axis episode title (Customer experience storyline: <location>) carry the correct identification.
